data.description:
## Why
An agent that needs a clean login currently shares the operator's browser profile, or asks for a click through the profile UI. A CLI that can list, add, and select a profile makes that a socket call. Backlog item: B3.

## Evidence
- c11: `BrowserProfileStore` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e) is `Sources/Tabs/BrowserTab.swift:341`. It persists to UserDefaults `browserProfiles.v1` (`:344`). `createProfile(named:)` is `:377`. `renameProfile(id:to:)` is `:398`. `websiteDataStore(for:)` is `:429` and uses `WKWebsiteDataStore(forIdentifier:)`. There is no `clear` and no `delete`.
- c11: `c11 browser --help` (`CLI/c11.swift:10181-10239`) has no `profiles` subcommand and no `--profile` on `open`. `new-tab` and `new-area` take `--type` and `--url` (`:2352-2362`, `:2603-2615`) and do not take a profile.
- Upstream: cmux #318, with a profile CLI in #3770 and #8874.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §5 Profiles row. Fable and Astra both mark it if-time. Astra row 4.15: list, add, and explicit selection first. clear and delete of an in-use profile need a lifecycle rule. `c11-1.0.html` agrees if-time. The backlog keeps the full verb list at P2.

## Scope
In: `c11 browser profiles list|add|rename|clear|delete`, and `--profile <name|id>` on `c11 browser open` and on `new-tab` / `new-area` when `--type browser`. `list` and `add` and `rename` and `--profile` are the part that must work. `clear` and `delete` ship in the same PR only with the refusal rules below. Teach both in the c11-browser skill.
Out: non-interactive import (parked 4.16b). URL allowlist. Passkeys. Sharing a profile with Chrome. A modal confirmation. `NSAlert.runModal()` on any path an agent can hit wedges the app (C11-204). Destructive verbs take `--yes` on the CLI and otherwise exit with a message. They never open a dialog.

## Approach
Socket methods under `browser.profiles.*`, off the main-actor hot path except the small UserDefaults write, which is already how the store persists. `list` returns id, name, and whether any live tab uses it. `add` calls `createProfile`. `rename` calls `renameProfile` and refuses the built-in profile when `canRenameProfile` is false (`:76` in the store section). `delete` and `clear` refuse when a live tab uses the profile, and refuse the built-in default. `clear` removes website data for that store only. `delete` also removes the definition. `--profile` on open resolves a name or id and passes the UUID into the existing browser-tab constructor (`BrowserTab.swift` around `:2900-2908`, which already takes a profile id). Missing profile is `not_found`, not a silent fallback to the default. Update `skills/c11-browser` and sync that installed skill.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `c11 browser profiles add smoke-b3` creates a profile, and `list --json` shows it. `rename smoke-b3 smoke-b3b` changes the name. A second `add` of the same name returns a clear error and does not create a duplicate.
2. `c11 browser open https://example.com --profile smoke-b3b` opens a tab whose profile id is that profile. A second open without `--profile` does not use smoke-b3b. Confirm with `list` showing which profile the new tab uses, or with the tab's metadata if the open response includes `profile_id`.
3. `c11 browser profiles delete smoke-b3b` while that tab is open exits non-zero and leaves the profile. After the tab is closed, `delete --yes smoke-b3b` removes it. Without `--yes`, delete does not remove it.
4. `clear --yes` on a profile that holds a cookie removes that cookie from a later navigation in that profile, and leaves another profile's cookies in place.
5. None of these commands changes the key window or opens a dialog.

## Validation
`tests_v2` against a tagged build for criteria 1, 2, 3, and 5. Criterion 4 needs a real web view. One computer-use or browser-skill check is enough. No soak. P2: if this misses the week-3 admission the backlog describes, it does not land in 1.0. Do not keep a half-finished clear/delete.

## Dependencies
None. B2's wizard smoke does not depend on this. Related only because both touch profiles. Feature flag `browser.profiles` if C6's list exists.

## Risks
Typing latency: none. Main thread: a profile-store write is small. Do not rebuild every web view on `list`. Doctrine: profiles are c11's own `WKWebsiteDataStore` identifiers. Do not write Chrome's, Arc's, or Safari's files, and do not write tenant config. Localization: new CLI errors and any new menu copy use `String(localized:)`. Six-locale fill is X1. Public repo: nothing sensitive. `clear` and `delete` are destructive. The in-use refusal is the guard.

Size: S–M. Tier: P2. Doctrine check: a profile is a c11 data store the caller names. Destructive verbs do not guess, and they do not modal.
data.title: Add browser profile list, add, rename, clear, delete, and --profile

Verdict: FAIL

C11-289 / PR #540, cycle 1. Reviewed HEAD 6d93b13a85d1d514435f5be491190d26bafcb6ef against merge-base 1e7d47ae70bbd1a7ae5868ad4c257d3eef1ceb5f (fresh origin/main). Detached checkout clean. Reviewed the full 16-file diff, ticket, plan, validation comment, and unchanged parsing, profile selection, persistence, history, UI switching, and socket-dispatch seams. Findings below are source-grounded; no builds, tests, or app runs performed by this reviewer.

Blocking

1. [P1] Explicit empty profile selection silently uses the operator's existing profile. Sources/SocketHandlers/BrowserHandlers.swift:1394; also Sources/SocketHandlers/SurfaceHandlers.swift:446 and Sources/SocketHandlers/PaneHandlers.swift:195. With an unset profile variable, `c11 browser open https://example.com --profile ""` sends an explicit empty string. `v2String` (Sources/TerminalController.swift:2911) converts that to nil, and the resolver's `.none` branch proceeds with normal workspace/global profile selection. Whitespace-only values do the same; non-string socket values are also treated as omitted. The command can therefore navigate with the operator's authenticated cookies instead of refusing an invalid isolation target. This violates the plan's explicit-selection/no-silent-fallback contract. Smallest fix: distinguish an absent profile key from a present invalid/empty value at all three creation endpoints, returning a localized invalid_params/not_found error before creating anything. Validate missing option values in the CLI as well. Add behavior cases asserting nonzero/error and no new tab for empty, whitespace, and malformed explicit selection; omission must retain existing behavior.

2. [P1] Destructive parsing discards target words and unknown flags. CLI/c11.swift:7813 and :7833. `add` joins positional words into a name, but `clear`/`delete` select only the first word and never reject leftovers. Given unused profiles named `smoke-b3` and `smoke-b3 extra`, `c11 browser profiles delete smoke-b3 extra --yes` deletes `smoke-b3`, leaving the intended multiword profile intact. Additionally, `delete smoke-b3 --yes --dry-run` discards the unsupported flag and actually deletes the profile. The server cannot catch this because it receives an already-truncated valid name and confirm=true. This violates the review's wrong-profile-data guard and the plan's requirement that destructive verbs do not guess. Smallest fix: strictly validate destructive arguments before sending the request, reject unknown flags and surplus/conflicting targets, and require exactly one target (a quoted name or UUID). Preserve the explicit --yes requirement. Add CLI behavior cases showing these malformed invocations leave both definitions and their data untouched.

Non-blocking

1. The shipped smoke's successful rename case renames PROFILE_A to PROFILE_A and checks only the id (tests_v2/test_browser_profiles.py:126). It cannot demonstrate AC1's actual name change. Rename to a distinct unused name and verify old-name rejection, new-name resolution, and unchanged UUID.
2. BrowserProfileStoreLifecycleTests:155 exercises a held clear and a second clear, but never attempts creation or switching while reserved. The timeout case at :188 never releases its held callback, so it does not demonstrate late completion. These do not cover the plan's complete delayed clear/delete scenario. Use the existing removal seam to exercise the named admission and late-completion cases in the Validator batch; no additional lifecycle mechanism is requested.

Runtime proof still required

The owner's validation event ev_01M3YR9HTFEHG3494G61STD2FH reports Atlas compilation, 2385 logic tests, two lifecycle tests, and a live cookie-isolation smoke at d83db59afcaa1aad2b7207ee3b8e3d7e19b8520c. Independently verified that only CLAUDE.md and skills/c11-computer-use/SKILL.md differ between that SHA and the reviewed head; product/test source is identical. The runtime results themselves were not independently rerun. PR checks were still running when inspected.

After repair, Atlas validation must demonstrate:

1. Empty/whitespace/malformed --profile and socket profile values fail without tab creation on browser open, new-tab, and new-area; valid explicit selection remains one-shot and unknown names fail.
2. Surplus targets and unknown flags on clear/delete fail without changing either synthetic profile or its cookies/history; correctly quoted multiword targets operate only on the named profile.
3. The existing smoke with an actual rename, clear/delete confirmation and built-in/in-use refusals, cross-profile cookie isolation, and unchanged key window/no dialog.
4. The plan's held-removal scenario for both clear and delete: attempted open/switch and duplicate destruction while pending, another profile remaining usable, no early success, bounded pending response, and completion after timeout finishing cleanup and releasing the reservation.

C11-289 is outside the mandatory pre-merge runtime risk list. Deferred Validator runtime proof alone is not the reason for FAIL; the two concrete targeting defects above are. CI must also complete on the repaired head before landing.

The Atlas smoke confirms both synthetic profiles' definitions, cookie stores, and persisted history remain unchanged after rejected invocations; quoted multiword rename/clear/delete target only the selected profile.

Blocking

None.

1. Round-1 empty-profile fallback is repaired. The dictionary-based resolver distinguishes omission from explicit empty, whitespace, non-string, and null values and rejects invalid values before creation. Browser open, tab.create, and area.create all use it. Unknown names still return not_found. CLI creation paths validate empty/missing/duplicate/flag-like selectors rather than silently omitting them. Omitted selection retains the prior behavior.
2. Round-1 destructive parsing is repaired. The dedicated parser requires exactly one positional or --profile target, rejects conflicting/duplicate selectors, surplus words, unknown flags, and duplicate --yes, and preserves confirmation_required when --yes is omitted. A quoted multiword name remains one target. No destructive socket call occurs on parser refusal.

Non-blocking

No new findings. Both prior test observations were addressed: rename now changes the name and checks UUID/name resolution; delayed clear and delete tests exercise reservation, duplicate refusal, attempted open/switch, another usable profile, bounded timeout, and late cleanup completion.

Mutation proof

Independently performed on Atlas through the repository's build-slot admission and build-lock scripts. No build, test, or app launch ran on Hyperion. The mutation was confined to a temporary copy of the exact-head native CLI sources; the owner checkout and its packaged app were not edited.

Exercised the unchanged tests_v2/test_browser_profiles.py::_run_cli_expect_failure assertion with its existing malformed_destructive case:

`browser profiles delete smoke-b3 --yes --dry-run`

Used an isolated Unix socket fixture that records requests and acknowledges a destructive request if received. It contains no real profiles or user data. This is CLI parser/request-admission proof, not a WebKit cleanup run.

Result: MUTATION_KILLED_AND_BASELINE_RESTORED. The server-side selector guard was source-reviewed and covered by the owner's live tests; it was not separately mutation-tested in this pass. Local review evidence directory: /tmp/c11-289-review-r2 (results.json, mutation.txt, c11-289-review-mutation.log, reproduce.py, review.md).

Runtime proof still required

Independently inspected Atlas result manifests for build invocation 5c74946cc5c7424c8371decbf3356bed and test invocation baefaf99e0c444ffa5985b87f30042a6. Both identify this exact head with no dirty overlay. Owner validation event ev_01M3YVEW5WHNEWJJSA7C28JEZ8 additionally reports the exact-head live tagged smoke passing against actual WebKit stores, malformed-command cookie/history preservation, and stable window identity. Semantic review
- `--profile` is a one-shot browser-tab creation selector. `browser.cookies.clear` and `browser.state.load` use the explicit/selected tab, whose BrowserTab WebView configuration owns the selected profile website-data store. State load writes cookies to that tab cookie store and storage to that tab WebView.
- `browser.profiles.clear` obtains the same profile WKWebsiteDataStore, removes all website data types, and clears that profile history. `browser.cookies.clear` removes only matching cookies from the targeted tab store. Same underlying store; intentionally different clearing scope. No fix was needed.
